items.title: Butch Miles interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, October 9, 2020 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: You’ve got brush work, Clayton Cameron, the great Clayton Cameron on brushes.

ctx.x: It is changing quite a bit. It’s in the process right now, Monk, of changing a lot. When I first started learning all about drums and drumsets, there were just a couple of books that were my method of manuals that may teacher had supplied me and was giving me lessons out of. They didn’t go very far. They weren’t really adaptable to the drumset. But this is because I started taking lessons back in the late 50s, you know around 1957, ’58, and there wasn’t a whole lot of material. Things have changed and improved so…

that, bless his heart, the great Jim Chapin. Or you have all other kinds of folks, one of the graduates from North Texas, one of the funkiest drummers in the world, Mr. Rick Latham, wrote an entire, a number of manuals about funk drumming. You’ve got brush work, Clayton Cameron, the great Clayton Cameron on brushes. You’ve got Ed Thigpen on brushes. You’ve got all sorts of wonderful manuals and drum methods now that are workable and usable, and they’re written by people who actually can play that. But it’s going…
